source.title: Adam+: A Stochastic Method with Adaptive Variance Reduction
source.authors: Mingrui Liu; W. Zhang; F. Orabona; Tian-Bao Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer training outcomes on natural-data tasks using held-out metrics, but does not test the original memorization, width, architecture, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on four tasks. The claim-relevant held-out comparisons are stated qualitatively in the text; curves are also shown in figures. The reported growth of Adam+’s gradient-estimator norm is an optimization diagnostic, not a measure of the train-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and nonadaptive optimizers using training and held-out performance under limited hyperparameter tuning, the method relevant to V4. Its new optimizer is not itself sufficient evidence for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially accurate. The authors claim Adam+ consistently beats Adam across the tested tasks and reaches performance comparable to well-tuned SGD or momentum SGD. They establish adaptive convergence guarantees and interpret slow cumulative gradient-estimator-norm growth as evidence explaining Adam+'s practical convergence speed.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a new optimizer, Adam+, against Adam, SGD, momentum SGD, Adagrad, and NIGT on image classification, language modeling, and speech recognition. It is not a direct reproduction of the cited adaptive-optimizer generalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and architecture differ across CIFAR10 ResNet18, CIFAR100 VGG19, WikiText-2 two-layer LSTM, and SWB-300 six-layer bidirectional LSTM; the language-model experiment uses dropout ratio 0.5. Optimizer tuning differs by task.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam+'s cumulative gradient-estimator norms plateau and subsequently grow slowly on the image tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slow growth of Adam+'s gradient-estimator norms is associated with its practical optimization convergence; this does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or a generalization gap.

record.problems: Held-out optimizer comparisons are largely qualitative or shown in figures without exact values. The text does not explicitly report Adam-versus-SGD results for the image and speech tasks, nor uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and conditions where Adam outperforms SGD. Adam-versus-SGD image results cannot be resolved from the supplied figure text.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Record the training-performance comparison accompanying R5: Adam has lower training perplexity than Adam+, which is comparable to SGD and momentum SGD. This supplies the training side of V4's train-versus-test pattern.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text preserves axes and legends but not readable curve trajectories. Image-task Adam-versus-SGD verdicts therefore remain unresolved. The language and speech conclusions use qualitative comparisons stated in the text; the speech result extends beyond V4's named image and language benchmarks. No uncertainty estimates establish the precision of these comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models; other image and language benchmarks.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: WikiText-2, two-layer LSTM, dropout 0.5, 40 epochs, learning-rate tuning with Adam's default moment parameters
relationships.reason: R5 matches the claimed pattern: Adam trains better but generalizes poorly; Section 3.2's Adam+ comparison qualitatively places SGD ahead of Adam on test perplexity.
relationships.display_finding: Qualitative comparisons through Adam+ suggested worse test perplexity for Adam than SGD despite better training performance.
